caveats: Unpaired, single-batch, n=6 vs n=6 design is underpowered for subtle compositional shifts; treat all findings here as hypothesis-generating

constraints: Do not use parametric tests (t-test/ANOVA) as the primary test given the small n per group without a normality check; Wilcoxon is the default, report normality check results if a parametric test is also shown

States explicitly that n=6 per arm in a single batch gives limited power, and that a non-significant result after FDR correction cannot be read as evidence of no biological difference

plan.title: Bulk RNA-seq immune/stromal deconvolution in anti-PD-1 melanoma
plan.analytical_narrative: The core delivered only a gene-level TPM table (12000 genes x 12 samples, Salmon-derived, human symbols) for a 6 treated vs 6 control anti-PD-1 melanoma design, with no raw counts and no quant directories. This rules out any count-based method (DESeq2/edgeR) and any tool that requires raw counts for its internal normalization (e.g. CIBERSORTx absolute mode, standard TIMER). Deconvolution from TPM is the correct and intended entry point: MCP-counter, quanTIseq, EPIC and xCell were all designed to run on TPM/FPKM-like continuous expression and are the standard toolkit for this exact question (Sturm et al. 2019 Bioinformatics benchmark; Finotello 2019 Genome Medicine for quanTIseq; Racle & Gfeller 2020 for EPIC; Becht 2016 for MCP-counter; Aran 2017 for xCell). All four algorithms plus the immunedeconv wrapper are installed in this sandbox (R GitHub track), matching the recommended multi-method approach rather than relying on a single algorithm's assumptions. Because the four methods report scores on different scales (MCP-counter: arbitrary units, not proportions; quanTIseq/EPIC: cell fractions; xCell: enrichment scores), the plan runs them in parallel, does not force them into one number, and only rank/z-score-normalizes within a method for cross-sample comparison. The known caveat that sample_01 was sequenced at ~1/4 median depth is carried through explicitly: low depth degrades all deconvolution equally (thinner counts per gene shift TPM estimates for lowly expressed marker genes), so this sample's outputs are flagged rather than excluded, and results are checked with and without it. Since n=6 per arm is small and unpaired, the treated-vs-control comparison for each cell type uses a non-parametric two-group test (Wilcoxon rank-sum, not requiring normality) with explicit FDR correction across the ~8-10 cell types tested per method, and results are reported as exploratory given the sample size. A checkpoint/cytotoxicity gene-signature scoring step (ssGSEA/singscore on hallmark and immunologic MSigDB gene sets, both present in the reference store) supplements deconvolution with an orthogonal, marker-independent read on immune activity, and a heatmap/PCA-style overview step gives per-sample composition profiles the question explicitly asks for ('every sample'). No raw counts, no reference single-cell atlas dataset, and no matched flow/IHC ground truth exist in this environment, so results are compositional estimates from bulk TPM, not validated cell counts — this is stated as a limitation, not silently assumed away.
